title: The Vvaan Crosses Rs 50 Crore in Week One Despite Drishyam 3 Arriving
excerpt: Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah's fantasy thriller crossed Rs 50 crore net in India in its first week, with Rs 69.07 crore worldwide — just as Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 opened to challenge it.
body:
• Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah's fantasy thriller The Vvaan crossed the Rs 50 crore net mark in India within its first week, collecting Rs 4.40 crore on Day 7 across 6,966 shows.
  • Total India net stands at Rs 53.50 crore with a worldwide gross of Rs 69.07 crore, including Rs 5.50 crore from overseas.
  • Trade analyst Taran Adarsh noted the film's strong acceptance in mass circuits and its steady weekday hold, aided by discounted ticket rates.
  • Week 2 will be the real test: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 released today (October 2), but a holiday Friday is expected to cushion The Vvaan.

Rs 50 Crore in Seven Days

The Vvaan has done what Bollywood's recent fantasy experiments have often struggled to do — hold its ground. Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah's fantasy thriller crossed the Rs 50 crore net mark at the domestic box office within seven days of release, pulling in Rs 4.40 crore net on Day 7 alone across 6,966 shows, per Sacnilk data.

Total India gross now stands at Rs 63.57 crore, with India net at Rs 53.50 crore. Overseas, the film added Rs 0.50 crore on Day 7, taking its overseas gross to Rs 5.50 crore and pushing the worldwide total to Rs 69.07 crore.

"TheVvaan is all set to hit the ₹50 cr mark in Week 1, thus emerging as a success story... The film stayed super-steady on Tuesday, getting that extra push from the discounted ticket rates."

— Taran Adarsh, trade analyst

Context & Background

Directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra — best known as the creator of the beloved series Panchayat — The Vvaan marks a significant genre departure for Hindi cinema's mainstream. The fantasy thriller stars Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah in the lead roles, with Anup Soni, Sunil Grover, Shweta Tiwari and Maniesh Paul in supporting parts. It is produced by Shobha Kapoor, Ekta Kapoor, Arunabh Kumar and Niraj Kothari, with Balaji Motion Pictures, TVF Motion Pictures and 11:11 Productions backing the project.

The film's run is particularly noteworthy for where it has found its audience. Adarsh observed that the film "has found strong acceptance in the mass circuits, which have continued to deliver very well even on weekdays" — a crucial signal, since mass-belt audiences have been the most volatile segment of Hindi box office demand in recent years, making or breaking mid-budget releases.

Impact & Analysis

The day-7 numbers matter because of how they were earned. A weekday hold of Rs 4.40 crore, with discounted ticket pricing in play, suggests genuine audience interest rather than front-loaded opening-weekend hype. For a fantasy thriller — a genre Hindi cinema has treated cautiously compared to its southern counterparts — the steady trajectory is a data point the industry will study.

The bigger question is Week 2. Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 — the conclusion of one of Bollywood's most successful thriller franchises — opened in theatres today. Competition for screens and single-screen audiences will be intense. But the timing offers The Vvaan one advantage: Friday, October 2, is a holiday, and Adarsh expects it to "ensure that The Vvaan continues to score despite the stiff competition."

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, The Vvaan's numbers carry a familiar narrative weight. Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah are both stars with strong overseas followings — Tamannaah's pan-Indian appeal after her southern cinema dominance has made her a draw for NRI audiences from Edison to East Ham. The Rs 5.50 crore overseas gross may look modest next to the domestic total, but overseas collections increasingly determine whether mid-budget Hindi films get their sequels and franchise extensions. With Balaji and TVF's production muscle behind it, a sustained overseas run could position The Vvaan as exactly the kind of original-IP success Bollywood has been hunting for — and diaspora box offices in the Gulf, North America and the UK will be decisive in the next two weeks.

What's Next

Week 2 will decide whether The Vvaan becomes a genuine success story or a one-week wonder. The Drishyam 3 clash will split screens and attention, and weekday holds from Monday onward will reveal the film's real legs. If the mass circuits keep delivering, crossing Rs 75–80 crore domestically is within reach — a result that would greenlight the kind of big-tent fantasy filmmaking Bollywood has been hesitant to commit to.
